title: Fresh-Challenge Vdf Attestations For Model-Relative Response Latency
authors: Aruzhan Tlessova Ansar Yesmukhanov
abstract: ArXiv:2609.12727v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Can a finite verifier obtain public, model-relative evidence about response latency for sequential computation? Verifiable delay functions (VDFs) make this possible in principle: evaluation requires T sequential steps, whereas verification is efficient in the security parameter and polylogarithmic in the numerical value of T for standard constructions. Thus a delay can be astronomically large to evaluate yet succinctly represented and feasibly checked. A VDF proof for a chosen message alone is insufficient because it may be precomputed. We specify and analyze Fresh-Challenge VDF Attestations (FCLA), a protocol composition that binds a VDF to an unpredictable public challenge, a message, and independently auditable release and receipt records. Under explicit assumptions about VDF sequentiality, the challenge source, witness logs, and a calibrated upper bound on an adversary's sequential evaluation rate, an accepted FCLA transcript is inconsistent with post-challenge generation by an adversary in that bounded model. The result neither identifies a named claimant nor excludes relaying, outsourcing, or a faster unmodeled machine. A benchmark of the public reference implementation confirms the expected empirical separation between evaluation and verification on one documented machine. Our contribution is a protocol/design analysis and benchmarked reference implementation layer, not a new VDF construction or cryptographic primitive.
tldr: The paper specifies Fresh-Challenge VDF Attestations (FCLA), a protocol that binds verifiable delay function proofs to unpredictable public challenges and auditable records to provide model-relative evidence of response latency.
motivation: A VDF proof for a chosen message can be precomputed, so it does not by itself prove that computation occurred after a request; a fresh, unpredictable challenge is needed to attest real sequential delay.
method: The authors introduce a protocol composition combining a VDF with a public challenge, message, and independently auditable release/receipt logs, and analyze it under assumptions about VDF sequentiality, challenge unpredictability, witness logs, and a bounded adversary evaluation rate.
result: Under those assumptions, an accepted FCLA transcript is inconsistent with post-challenge generation by the adversary in the bounded model, and a reference implementation benchmark confirms empirical separation between evaluation and verification on one machine.
conclusion: The contribution is a protocol/design analysis and benchmarked reference implementation, not a new VDF construction, and it does not identify a named claimant or rule out relaying, outsourcing, or unmodeled faster machines.

title: Diagonal Pair Coulomb Density Matrix On A Sphere: A Numerical Study
authors: Riccardo Fantoni
abstract: ArXiv:2609.11984v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We tabulate, on the diagonal, the [MATH]th power of the primitive approximation for the pair Coulomb density matrix on a sphere, with up to [MATH], and we discuss its behavior at particles contact as [MATH] grows. Our results show that even on a curved surface quantum statistical physics is fundamentally different from its classical counterpart. If in the latter one needs to artificially introduce a regularization of the divergent attractive Coulomb potential preventing particles contact, for example with a hard core, in the former this is not necessary.
tldr: A numerical study tabulating the diagonal primitive approximation for the pair Coulomb density matrix on a sphere and examining its contact behavior.
motivation: To understand whether quantum statistical physics on a curved surface differs fundamentally from its classical counterpart, particularly regarding the need to regularize the attractive Coulomb potential.
method: The authors compute the diagonal elements of the Mth power of the primitive approximation for the pair Coulomb density matrix on a sphere, up to some maximum M, and analyze the behavior as particles come into contact.
result: They find that on a curved surface, unlike in the classical case, no artificial regularization such as a hard core is necessary to prevent particles from contacting each other.
conclusion: Quantum statistical physics on a sphere exhibits qualitative differences from classical statistical physics, removing the need for ad hoc contact regularization.

title: A Finite Data Based Regularization In A Normed Linear Space Setting
authors: M. Thamban Nair
abstract: ArXiv:2609.11960v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: One of the basic problems in mathematical learning theory is to identify a function [MATH] with certain specific properties which fits a given training data [MATH], in the sense that, [MATH] for [MATH], where [MATH] is a compact subset of [MATH] for some [MATH] and [MATH] is required to have certain specified characteristics. We address this problem when [MATH] belongs to an arbitrary normed linear space [MATH], and the evaluation maps [MATH] are replaced by maps of the form [MATH] on [MATH], where [MATH] are continuous linear functionals on [MATH]. Using an inner product structure on [MATH], we shall device a method of least-squares for obtaining an approximate solution for the above problem and also identify a subspace of [MATH] in which the least-square solution is unique, which in turn is shown to be equivalent to solving a matrix equation. In the context when the matrix under consideration is ill-conditioned, a regularized equation is devised, and order optimal error estimates are derived for the exact targeted data [MATH] and also when it is noisy, by choosing the regularization parameter appropriately.
tldr: The paper develops a least-squares regularization framework for finite-data function fitting when the hypothesis space is an arbitrary normed linear space with evaluation maps given by continuous linear functionals.
motivation: Basic problems in mathematical learning theory require fitting training data with functions having prescribed properties, but standard treatments assume Hilbert spaces or point-evaluation maps, limiting generality.
method: By imposing an inner product structure on the normed linear space, the authors formulate a least-squares problem, identify a subspace where the solution is unique and equivalent to a matrix equation, and introduce a regularized equation for ill-conditioned matrices.
result: Order-optimal error estimates are derived for both exact and noisy target data, with the regularization parameter chosen appropriately to control the ill-conditioning of the matrix.
conclusion: The work generalizes regularization theory for learning to arbitrary normed linear spaces with linear functional evaluations, providing optimal convergence guarantees, but remains purely classical mathematical learning theory.

title: Frequency-Multiplexed Photonic Reservoir Computing With A Synchronously Pulse-Driven Optical Cavity
authors: Amir Arsalan Arabieh, Simon-Pierre Gorza, Serge Massar
abstract: ArXiv:2609.12212v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we introduce a new platform for frequency-multiplexed reservoir computing based on an optical cavity driven by pulses whose repetition period is matched to the cavity roundtrip time. The input symbols are encoded by modulating either the amplitude or the phase of the driving pulses. Our numerical results show that the proposed synchronously pulse-driven cavity operates in a weakly nonlinear regime under anomalous dispersion, while under normal dispersion it exhibits optical bistability with a high-peak-power upper-branch state. By isolating the key physical parameters, we quantify their individual contributions to information-processing performance. We further show that spectral symmetry breaking induced by third-order dispersion and Raman scattering almost doubles the information-processing capacity. Finally, we demonstrate that modulation-induced branch switching within the bistable regime limits stable reservoir operation.
tldr: The paper introduces a frequency-multiplexed photonic reservoir computing platform based on an optical cavity driven by pulses synchronized to the cavity roundtrip time, and numerically characterizes its information-processing performance.
motivation: Reservoir computing offers a simple training paradigm for temporal information processing, and photonic implementations promise high bandwidth; the authors seek a new cavity-based platform that exploits frequency multiplexing for greater capacity.
method: A synchronously pulse-driven optical cavity is modeled numerically, with input symbols encoded via amplitude or phase modulation of the driving pulses; key physical parameters (dispersion, nonlinearity, Raman scattering, third-order dispersion) are isolated and their contributions to information-processing capacity quantified.
result: The cavity operates weakly nonlinearly under anomalous dispersion and exhibits optical bistability with a high-peak-power upper branch under normal dispersion; spectral symmetry breaking from third-order dispersion and Raman scattering nearly doubles the information-processing capacity, while modulation-induced branch switching limits stable operation.
conclusion: Synchronously pulse-driven optical cavities are a viable route to frequency-multiplexed photonic reservoir computing, provided that branch-switching instabilities in the bistable regime are avoided.

title: Efficient Kinetic Monte Carlo Simulations With Long-range Electrostatic Interactions
authors: Roya Ebrahimi Viand, Bat-Amgalan Bat-Erdene, Karsten Reuter, Sebastian Matera
abstract: ArXiv:2609.12538v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Charge transport in solid-state materials is often governed by charge carrier hopping processes in the presence of long-range electrostatic interactions. Kinetic Monte Carlo (kMC) simulations provide a framework for describing such rare-event dynamics over extended timescales. However, the efficient treatment of long-range interactions remains a major computational challenge, since each particle jump modifies the energy landscape globally and, in principle, requires updating all transition rates after every carrier motion. We present an efficient and generally applicable update process for these transition rates in the presence of long-range electrostatic interactions. To illustrate the method, we study charge diffusion on a simple cubic host lattice under an external electric field. The transport behavior is investigated in high states of charge (SOC), and the influence of temperature, electric field strength, and SOC is examined. Our simulations show strongly suppressed transport at 100\,\% SOC (50\,\% occupation) caused by a freezing of the charge carriers into a Coulomb superlattice. Slight deviations from this reference in terms of charge carrier concentration lead to a rapid increase in conductivity. A deeper analysis reveals that this behavior can be rationalized as transport of non-interacting defects in the Coulomb superlattice. These results demonstrate the capability of the proposed update procedure to efficiently capture non-equilibrium transport phenomena in interacting charged systems and provide a foundation for simulations of more complex charge diffusion problems.
tldr: The paper presents an efficient transition-rate update scheme for kinetic Monte Carlo simulations of charge hopping with long-range electrostatic interactions, applied to charge diffusion on a cubic lattice under an external field.
motivation: Long-range electrostatic interactions make kMC simulations of charge transport computationally expensive because every particle jump globally alters the energy landscape and all transition rates.
method: The authors develop a generally applicable update procedure for transition rates under long-range electrostatics and test it on a simple cubic host lattice with an applied electric field, exploring temperature, field strength, and state of charge.
result: At 100% state of charge (50% occupation) transport is strongly suppressed due to freezing of carriers into a Coulomb superlattice, while slight concentration deviations yield a rapid conductivity increase attributable to non-interacting defect transport.
conclusion: The proposed update scheme efficiently captures non-equilibrium transport in interacting charged systems and provides a foundation for simulating more complex charge-diffusion problems.

title: Persistence Of Bkt Phase Transition In The 2d Nonanalytic Xy Model
authors: Sihan Hu, Xianzhi Pan, Kun Chen, Yi Jiang, Youjin Deng
abstract: ArXiv:2609.12560v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the two-dimensional XY model with the nonanalytic pair potential [MATH], whose small-angle law [MATH] carries a cusp for [MATH] and a flat bottom for [MATH], invalidating the harmonic spin-wave expansion. Two questions arise: the nature of the low-temperature ([MATH]) phase and of the phase transition. A naive energetic argument would predict genuine long-range order and an enhanced transition temperature for [MATH], and no transition at all for [MATH]. Large-scale Monte Carlo simulations contradict both: for every [MATH] the is quasi-long-range ordered, with anomalous dimension [MATH], and terminates at a Berezinskii--Kosterlitz--Thouless transition. Using a vortex-free noncompact lattice-field description and utilizing a duality transformation, we show that coarse-graining drives the height-difference distribution onto a single Gaussian fixed point, renormalizing the cusp and flatness into a finite harmonic stiffness that restores the spin-wave description and the BKT scenario for all [MATH].
tldr: Large-scale Monte Carlo simulations and a duality-based field description show that the 2D XY model with a nonanalytic pair potential still exhibits quasi-long-range order and a BKT transition for all cusp/flatness parameters.
motivation: The nonanalytic pair potential invalidates the harmonic spin-wave expansion, raising the question of whether the low-temperature phase and transition survive or are replaced by true long-range order or no transition.
method: The authors perform large-scale Monte Carlo simulations and use a vortex-free noncompact lattice-field description with a duality transformation to analyze coarse-graining of the height-difference distribution.
result: For every parameter value, the system remains quasi-long-range ordered with anomalous dimension η = 1/4 and terminates at a Berezinskii–Kosterlitz–Thouless transition; coarse-graining drives the distribution to a Gaussian fixed point with finite harmonic stiffness.
conclusion: The BKT scenario is robust against cusps and flat bottoms in the small-angle potential, as renormalization restores an effective spin-wave description.

title: Nonexistence Of Approximately Dual Frames Via Weighted Composition Operators
authors: Trevor Camper, Dongwei Chen, Shuang Guan
abstract: ArXiv:2609.12357v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reconstruction from the coefficients of a frame often requires a dual frame, and the canonical dual is obtained by inverting the frame operator, which is rarely available in a closed form. It is therefore natural to ask whether the duality can instead be implemented by an operator of prescribed form. We study this problem in the context of weighted composition operators on Hardy and Bargmann-Fock spaces. We first characterize those weighted composition operators which carry a frame together with a dual of it to another such pair. We then prove that if the image of a frame under a weighted composition operator is itself a dual frame, then such an operator is a positive scalar multiple of the identity and the frame is tight on both Hardy and Bargmann-Fock spaces. Relaxing duality to approximate duality, we show that on the Hardy space, composition is still forced to be the identity under mild regularity for the weight function. Approximate tightness, however, fails completely. On the Bargmann-Fock space, the situation is rigid: such an approximate dual exists precisely when the ratio of the optimal frame bounds does not exceed an explicit sharp threshold determined by the prescribed error.
tldr: The paper studies when weighted composition operators on Hardy and Bargmann-Fock spaces can implement exact or approximate duality of frames, showing rigidity results and explicit thresholds.
motivation: Reconstructing signals from frame coefficients usually requires a dual frame, and the canonical dual (via inversion of the frame operator) is seldom available in closed form, motivating the search for duals implemented by operators of a prescribed form.
method: The authors characterize weighted composition operators that map a frame and its dual to another such pair, and then analyze the cases where the image of a frame is itself a dual or approximately dual frame on Hardy and Bargmann-Fock spaces.
result: Exact duality forces the operator to be a positive scalar multiple of the identity with a tight frame, and approximate duality on the Hardy space still forces the composition to be the identity under mild regularity, while on Bargmann-Fock space an approximate dual exists exactly when the ratio of optimal frame bounds is below an explicit sharp threshold.
conclusion: Duality and approximate duality of frames are extremely rigid under weighted composition operators on these analytic function spaces, with approximate tightness failing entirely in general.

title: Division Algebras, Triality, And Exceptional Magic
authors: A. Garrett Lisi
abstract: ArXiv:2609.12112v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We describe in explicit detail the rich relationship between division algebras, split composition algebras, triality, Clifford algebras, spinors, triality Lie algebras, generalized reflections, exceptional magic square Lie algebras, triality eigenspaces, 3-symmetric spaces, Vinberg theta algebras, and Exceptional Unification in particle physics.
tldr: The paper provides an explicit mathematical exposition of the relationships between division algebras, triality, Clifford algebras, spinors, and exceptional Lie algebras in the context of particle physics unification.
motivation: To elucidate the algebraic structures underlying exceptional unification in particle physics and to detail the deep connections between division algebras, triality, and Clifford algebras.
method: Explicit construction and analysis of division algebras, split composition algebras, triality, Clifford algebras, spinors, triality Lie algebras, generalized reflections, exceptional magic square Lie algebras, and Vinberg theta algebras.
result: A comprehensive description of how these algebraic structures interrelate, including triality eigenspaces, 3-symmetric spaces, and their role in exceptional unification.
conclusion: The work offers a unified algebraic framework that may be relevant to particle physics unification but has no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Inverse Reconstruction Of Dissipative Kerr Soliton Interactions
authors: Carlo Silvestri, Panayotis G. Kevrekidis, Stephane Coen, C. Martijn de Sterke, Antoine F. J. Runge
abstract: ArXiv:2609.12269v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We reconstruct the pairwise interaction potential between dissipative Kerr solitons from the linear stability spectrum of a perfect soliton crystal solution of the Lugiato--Lefever equation. The solitons form an overdamped lattice whose positional eigenvalues encode the pairwise-force derivative, mirroring the extraction of microscopic interactions from phonon or relaxation spectra in condensed-matter systems. The method extends beyond quadratic dispersion and assumes no functional form for the interaction. Our theory predicts a novel state -the soft soliton crystal- which has vanishing stiffness and a diverging positional relaxation time, and also explains experimentally observed soliton steps as arising from a sign reversal of the pairwise-force derivative.
tldr: The paper reconstructs the pairwise interaction potential between dissipative Kerr solitons from the linear stability spectrum of a soliton crystal in the Lugiato-Lefever equation.
motivation: Dissipative Kerr solitons form ordered lattices in driven nonlinear cavities, but the microscopic pairwise forces governing their arrangement were not directly extractable from spectral data.
method: The authors treat the perfect soliton crystal as an overdamped lattice and invert its positional linear-stability eigenvalues to recover the derivative of the pairwise force, without assuming a functional form and going beyond quadratic dispersion.
result: The inversion predicts a novel 'soft soliton crystal' state with vanishing stiffness and diverging positional relaxation time, and explains experimentally observed soliton steps as arising from a sign reversal of the pairwise-force derivative.
conclusion: Inverse reconstruction of soliton interactions offers a spectroscopy-like tool for soliton crystals, analogous to extracting microscopic interactions from phonon or relaxation spectra in condensed-matter systems.

title: Quasi-exactly Solvable Deformations Of Quantum Systems Associated With Exceptional Orthogonal Polynomials
authors: Siyu Li, Ian Marquette, Sarah Post, Yao-Zhong Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.12428v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quasi-exactly solvable (QES) deformations of harmonic and singular oscillators have been widely studied via a range of approaches. In this paper, we obtain families of new QES deformations of solvable quantum systems associated with exceptional orthogonal polynomials (EOPs). The construction builds upon the theory of Darboux-Crum transformations and the classification of exactly solvable quantum systems associated with EOPs of Hermite type. It is shown that the deformations break the exact solvability of the undeformed systems and introduce model parameters into the deformed systems that permit the existence of a finite number of polynomial solutions whose roots satisfy systems of algebraic equations. The new families presented and studied consist of deformations of quantum systems related to Hermite EOPs of type III with arbitrary codimensions. We present polynomial and rational deformations and analyze, in each case, the conditions for quasi-exact solvability in terms of Bethe ansatz equations and parameter constraints. In general, the structures of the underlying polynomial solutions are no longer associated with well-known classical orthogonal polynomials. So for the general cases, we mainly focus on presenting the new approach as well as the Bethe ansatz equations and the constraints for model parameters. As applications, we construct particular families of QES deformations related to solvable models allowing one, two, and up to four gaps, and obtain the closed form expressions for their wavefunctions and spectra. We analyze the existence of QES solutions in the spaces of model parameters, providing information on the number of solutions for given parameters.
tldr: The paper constructs new quasi-exactly solvable (QES) deformations of harmonic and singular oscillators using exceptional orthogonal polynomials (EOPs) and Darboux-Crum transformations.
motivation: QES deformations of solvable quantum systems have been widely studied, but families of deformations tied to exceptional orthogonal polynomials of Hermite type III with arbitrary codimension had not been systematically developed.
method: The authors build on Darboux-Crum transformation theory and the classification of exactly solvable systems associated with Hermite-type EOPs, deriving polynomial and rational deformations and characterizing quasi-exact solvability via Bethe ansatz equations and parameter constraints.
result: They obtain new families of QES deformations of Hermite EOP type III systems with arbitrary codimension, including solvable models with one to four gaps, with closed-form wavefunctions and spectra and an analysis of QES solution counts in parameter space.
conclusion: The work extends the theory of QES systems to EOP-based deformations, providing a general framework and explicit examples, though the resulting polynomial structures generally cease to be classical orthogonal polynomials.

title: Prior-information Based Super-resolution Optical Metrology Of 2d Nanoscale Objects
authors: Jin-Kyu So, Eng Aik Chan, Carolina Rend\'on-Barraza, Giorgio Adamo, Nikolay I. Zheludev
abstract: ArXiv:2609.12671v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Previous work has shown that optical metrology of one-dimensional objects, such as slit width, can achieve improved accuracy by using prior information from similar objects to train the metrology estimator. Here, we demonstrate single-shot optical metrology of nanoscale elliptical particles by analysing their diffraction patterns to retrieve length, width and in-plane orientation using a neural-network estimator trained on prior information from nano-ellipses with varied dimensions and orientations. Fisher-information flow analysis was used to optimise the physical parameters of the metrology apparatus and maximise measurement accuracy. Using a 633 nm laser, we measure the dimensions of elliptical particles with accuracy down to [MATH]/128, corresponding to 4.9 nm, and recover their orientation with 5[MATH] accuracy. Our results demonstrate the practicality of optical, deep-super-resolution, single-shot, multiparameter measurements of two-dimensional subwavelength objects, with potential relevance to microbiology and nanotechnology applications.
tldr: The paper demonstrates single-shot optical metrology of nanoscale elliptical particles using a neural-network estimator trained on prior information and optimized via Fisher-information flow analysis.
motivation: Previous work showed that prior information from similar objects can improve optical metrology of one-dimensional objects; this work extends that idea to two-dimensional subwavelength objects.
method: Diffraction patterns from nano-ellipses are analyzed with a neural-network estimator trained on varied dimensions and orientations, while Fisher-information flow is used to optimize the optical apparatus parameters.
result: Using a 633 nm laser, the authors retrieve length, width, and in-plane orientation with dimensions accurate to approximately 4.9 nm and orientation accuracy of about 5 degrees.
conclusion: The approach enables practical optical, deep-super-resolution, single-shot, multiparameter measurements of 2D subwavelength objects, with potential applications in microbiology and nanotechnology.

title: The Borel Complexity Of Conjugacy For Cantor Minimal Systems
authors: Xinan Dai, Wenhao Deng, Yingdong Shi, Tailin Wu, Yuchen Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.12031v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that conjugacy of minimal homeomorphisms of the Cantor space is Borel bireducible with isomorphism of countable graphs, answering the Cantor minimal case of a question of Foreman. We obtain the lower bound by encoding countably based profinite groups. Finite quotient homomorphisms are represented by factor maps between a common family of minimal subshifts. Amalgamation makes the resulting inverse limit independent, up to conjugacy, of the quotient presentation. Conversely, finite-stage factorization recovers the group from any conjugacy of these inverse limits.
tldr: The paper proves that conjugacy of minimal homeomorphisms of the Cantor space is Borel bireducible with isomorphism of countable graphs, resolving a case of Foreman's question.
motivation: The classification of Cantor minimal systems up to conjugacy is a central problem in topological dynamics and descriptive set theory, and this work aims to determine its exact Borel complexity.
method: The authors encode countably based profinite groups via finite quotient homomorphisms represented by factor maps between minimal subshifts, using amalgamation to make the inverse limit independent of the quotient presentation, and finite-stage factorization for the converse.
result: They show that conjugacy of minimal Cantor homeomorphisms is Borel bireducible with countable graph isomorphism, establishing the lower and upper bounds.
conclusion: This settles the Cantor minimal case of Foreman's question and places the classification problem at the same complexity level as countable graph isomorphism.

title: Thermodynamic Formalism Out Of Equilibrium Part Ii: Semi-Ruelle Operator, Conformal Measures, And Effective Expansion And Quasi-Compactness
authors: Snir Ben Ovadia
abstract: ArXiv:2609.12068v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a general machinery to study {\em thermodynamic formalism out of equilibrium}: The thermodynamics of a topological Markov shift (denoted by [MATH]) where the potential is given by a random walk on a compact metric space [MATH] (and the randomness is driven by a Gibbs process). We introduce the {\em semi-Ruelle operator}, which acts on [MATH]. We construct conformal measures and harmonic functions for the semi-Ruelle operator. We present a few applications: (1) We provide a new proof to the POE variational principle (POE stands for the {\em pressure out of equilibrium} which is associated with the process), and we show that maximizing measures in the POE variational principle admit positive {\em entropy out of equilibrium}, and satisfy {\em semi-Gibbs estimates}. (2) In the setting where the random walk on the fiber [MATH] is given by [MATH] diffeomorphisms (which are allowed to be very dissipative), and it satisfies the open condition of {\em effective expansion on average}, we show that the {\em averaged semi-Ruelle operator} is quasi-compact when acting on a Sobolev function space. An application includes proving a spectral gap when assuming volume decay of correlations, and proving bounds on the dimension of stationary measure in terms of similarity dimension.
tldr: The paper develops a general thermodynamic formalism out of equilibrium using a semi-Ruelle operator on a topological Markov shift with a random walk potential driven by a Gibbs process.
motivation: To extend thermodynamic formalism to non-equilibrium settings where the potential is given by a random walk on a compact metric space, and to study its ergodic and spectral properties.
method: Introduces the semi-Ruelle operator acting on a suitable function space and constructs conformal measures and harmonic functions; applies this to a variational principle for pressure out of equilibrium and to quasi-compactness of an averaged operator under effective expansion.
result: Provides a new proof of the POE variational principle, shows maximizing measures have positive entropy out of equilibrium and satisfy semi-Gibbs estimates, and proves quasi-compactness of the averaged semi-Ruelle operator on a Sobolev space, leading to spectral gaps and dimension bounds.
conclusion: The machinery offers a framework for studying thermodynamic formalism in random non-equilibrium settings, with applications to spectral gap and dimension estimates for stationary measures.

title: A Spectral-element Method For Computing Many Eigenvalues And Their Asymptotics Of The Schr\"odinger Operator With Robin Boundary Condition
authors: Fukeng Huang Weizhu Bao
abstract: ArXiv:2609.12369v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose spectral and spectral-element methods for accurately computing many eigenvalues of the Schr\"odinger operator with Robin boundary condition on simple and complex geometries, respectively. Due to their spectral-type accuracy in approximating those eigenfunctions corresponding to high-index eigenvalues, which are usually highly oscillatory, the proposed approaches have excellent resolution in computing thousands of eigenvalues accurately and efficiently with the resolution property that the number of eigenvalues with reasonable accuracy is proportional to the number of degrees of freedom. Using a standard HPC node with 128 GB of memory, we can obtain numerically more than 5,000 reliable eigenvalues with relative errors below [MATH] for different complex domains in two dimensions (2D). Based on these computed eigenvalues, we first confirm some theoretical results on the Robin-to-Neumann (RtN) gaps of the Laplacian operator in 2D, which were recently studied by Rudnick [ 388 (2021)]. Then we systematically study the RtN gaps of the Schr\"odinger operator and their convergence rates. Based on our extensive numerical results, we formulate a unified conjecture on the cumulative averages of the RtN gaps of the Schr\"odinger operator.
tldr: The paper develops spectral and spectral-element numerical methods for efficiently computing thousands of eigenvalues of the Schrödinger operator with Robin boundary conditions on 2D domains, and uses them to study Robin-to-Neumann gap asymptotics.
motivation: Accurately computing many high-index, highly oscillatory eigenvalues of Schrödinger operators is numerically challenging, yet such spectra underlie theoretical questions about eigenvalue gaps and their asymptotics.
method: The authors propose spectral and spectral-element discretizations that achieve spectral-type accuracy for oscillatory eigenfunctions, scaling the number of resolvable eigenvalues linearly with degrees of freedom, and validate them on simple and complex 2D geometries.
result: They compute over 5,000 reliable eigenvalues with small relative errors on a standard HPC node, confirm recent theoretical results on Laplacian Robin-to-Neumann gaps, and characterize the convergence rates of these gaps for the Schrödinger operator, leading to a unified conjecture.
conclusion: The proposed methods provide a scalable, high-accuracy tool for spectral computations and yield new numerical evidence and conjectures on Robin-to-Neumann gap statistics.

title: Early Stopping Of Stochastic Variance Reduced Gradient For Linear Inverse Problems By The Discrepancy Principle
authors: Zehui Zhou Bangti Jin
abstract: ArXiv:2609.12396v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Stochastic variance reduced gradient (SVRG) is a variant of stochastic gradient descent and is a promising iterative method for solving large-scale inverse problems. Nevertheless, the development of theoretically grounded a posteriori stopping rules for SVRG remains an open challenge. In this work, we provide a convergence analysis of SVRG equipped with the discrepancy principle, the most well-known a posteriori stopping rule, for solving a class of linear inverse problems in Hilbert spaces. We establish the regularizing property of SVRG, and moreover, under suitable source conditions, we derive convergence rates of SVRG iterates. To the best of our knowledge, these are the first convergence rate results of any stochastic iterative method for inverse problems under the a posteriori stopping rule. The theoretical findings are supported by numerical experiments.
tldr: The paper analyzes early stopping of stochastic variance reduced gradient (SVRG) for linear inverse problems using the discrepancy principle, establishing convergence rates under source conditions.
motivation: Stochastic iterative methods like SVRG are promising for large-scale inverse problems, but theoretically grounded a posteriori stopping rules are lacking.
method: The authors provide a convergence analysis of SVRG equipped with the discrepancy principle for linear inverse problems in Hilbert spaces, using source conditions to derive convergence rates.
result: They establish the regularizing property of SVRG and obtain the first convergence rate results for a stochastic iterative method for inverse problems under an a posteriori stopping rule, supported by numerical experiments.
conclusion: The discrepancy principle provides a rigorous early stopping strategy for SVRG in linear inverse problems, though the work is outside quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid quantum systems.

title: A Structural Relationship Between Crouzeix-Raviart Immersed Finite Elements For Elliptic And Stokes Interface Problems
authors: Jiaying Ren, Guozhu Yu, Xu Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.12462v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the structural relationship between immersed finite element (IFE) spaces for scalar elliptic and Stokes interface problems on unfitted meshes. Although IFE methods have been widely developed for individual partial differential equation models, the algebraic connection between scalar and vector IFE spaces has not been systematically explored. We establish a precise unisolvence relationship between the immersed Crouzeix-Raviart (CR) element for elliptic interface problems and the immersed CR-[MATH] element for Stokes interface problems in both gradient and stress formulations. By analyzing the block structure of the local IFE matrices, we show that the determinant of the Stokes IFE matrix factorizes in terms of the determinant of the corresponding elliptic IFE matrix. This factorization reveals an intrinsic algebraic link between the two classes of immersed elements and explains the unisolvence of the Stokes IFE spaces through the scalar elliptic case. The same result extends naturally to three dimensions and significantly simplifies the corresponding analysis. Numerical experiments confirm optimal convergence rates for both velocity and pressure in three-dimensional Stokes interface problems.
tldr: The paper establishes an algebraic unisolvence connection between Crouzeix-Raviart immersed finite element spaces for scalar elliptic and vector Stokes interface problems.
motivation: Immersed finite element methods have been developed separately for elliptic and Stokes interface problems, but the algebraic relationship between their scalar and vector spaces has not been systematically explored.
method: The authors analyze the block structure of local immersed finite element matrices and show that the determinant of the Stokes IFE matrix factorizes in terms of the determinant of the corresponding elliptic IFE matrix.
result: The factorization reveals an intrinsic algebraic link, explains the unisolvence of the Stokes IFE spaces via the scalar elliptic case, and extends naturally to three dimensions, with numerical experiments confirming optimal convergence for 3D Stokes interface problems.
conclusion: This structural relationship simplifies the analysis of immersed Crouzeix-Raviart elements for Stokes interface problems by reducing it to the scalar elliptic case.

title: Linear Exponential Quadratic Gaussian Covariance Steering
authors: Chiran B. Cherian, Yasemin Isik, Abhishek Halder
abstract: ArXiv:2609.12463v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We formulate and analyze the linear exponential quadratic Gaussian (LEQG) covariance steering problem in continuous time over a given deadline (finite time horizon). The solution for this problem can be seen as a risk-sensitive Schr\"{o}dinger bridge between Gaussian endpoints in the linear quadratic setting. Unlike the risk-neutral case, the LEQG covariance steering controller--still a linear state feedback--can no longer be written in closed form. We show that the optimal controller is parameterized by a symmetric matrix solving an algebraic equation that encodes the implicit dependence on the risk-sensitivity parameter. We explain how the structure of this optimal controller significantly generalizes the existing results for the risk-neutral case. Building on these results, for the matched noise and input channel case, we prove the existence-uniqueness of solution for the LEQG covariance steering problem in the neighborhood of the known risk-neutral optimal solution. We give an illustrative numerical example.
tldr: The paper formulates and analyzes the continuous-time linear exponential quadratic Gaussian (LEQG) covariance steering problem as a risk-sensitive Schrödinger bridge between Gaussian endpoints.
motivation: Covariance steering has been well-studied in the risk-neutral linear quadratic setting, but the risk-sensitive (exponential quadratic) case lacks a comparable framework and solution structure.
method: The optimal controller is shown to be linear state feedback parameterized by a symmetric matrix solving an algebraic equation that implicitly depends on the risk-sensitivity parameter; existence and uniqueness of the solution are proved near the known risk-neutral optimum for matched noise and input channels.
result: The derived controller significantly generalizes existing risk-neutral results, and a numerical example illustrates the approach.
conclusion: This work provides a foundation for risk-sensitive covariance steering and connects it to Schrödinger bridge problems, though it remains within control theory rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Confusion-Erasure Bounds Of Error-Bounded Decoders Under Qam
authors: Wenwen Chen, Bin Han, Hans D. Schotten
abstract: ArXiv:2609.12631v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: 6G is expected to push ultra-reliable low-latency communication (URLLC) toward stringent residual-error targets for mission-critical services, where undetected errors and erasures carry fundamentally different costs. Block error rate (BLER) conflates block confusions (undetected errors) and block erasures, which have fundamentally different impacts on system reliability. This paper extends the confusion and erasure analysis of error-bounded decoders to square quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM) constellations in the finite blocklength (FBL) regime. To handle QAM's heterogeneous symbol energies - which make the per-pair Euclidean distance a distribution rather than a single value - we derive analytical lower and upper bounds on the block confusion rate by, respectively, collapsing this distribution to its root-mean-square (RMS) distance and averaging the pairwise confusion over it. These bounds are proven to be monotonically decreasing in both the average symbol energy and the blocklength, with the decrease rate governed by the constellation order. Numerical results confirm that as the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) or redundancy increases, the confusion rate falls many orders of magnitude below the reliability target, leaving detectable erasures as the dominant residual error.
tldr: This paper derives analytical bounds on block confusion and erasure rates for error-bounded decoders under square QAM in the finite-blocklength regime, targeting 6G URLLC reliability.
motivation: Ultra-reliable low-latency communication for 6G requires distinguishing undetected errors (confusions) from detectable erasures, since they have different system-level costs and BLER alone conflates them.
method: The authors extend confusion-erasure analysis to QAM by handling heterogeneous symbol energies: lower bounds use RMS pairwise distance, upper bounds average pairwise confusion over the distance distribution, and monotonicity in average energy and blocklength is proven.
result: Numerical results show that as SNR or redundancy increases, confusion rates fall many orders of magnitude below reliability targets, making detectable erasures the dominant residual error source.
conclusion: The proposed bounds provide a refined reliability characterization for QAM-based error-bounded decoders, highlighting erasures rather than confusions as the limiting factor in the high-reliability regime.

title: Shuffling Is Not Enough: Breaking Permutation-Based Model Confidentiality In Hybrid Fhe Inference
authors: Hyung Tae Lee Jiseung Kim
abstract: ArXiv:2609.12911v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hybrid fully homomorphic encryption~(FHE) inference improves the practicality of private inference by letting the server evaluate linear layers homomorphically while the client decrypts and applies nonlinearities. Recent schemes attempt to protect model confidentiality by returning noisy, output-permuted responses and appealing to shuffle-model differential privacy~(DP). We show that this protection fails in the correctness regime required by hybrid FHE systems. For a [MATH]-input linear layer, [MATH] admissible queries suffice for exact recovery of a permutation-invariant layer summary, hence for perfect model distinguishability. We further show that input DP is orthogonal to model confidentiality and that the local-DP premise required for shuffle amplification cannot hold under correctness-bounded noise. We recover all linear layers of a \safhire{}-style ResNet-20 end-to-end from TFHE transcripts with zero error, using [MATH] queries per layer for a total of [MATH] direct queries. Under the same query model, we also confirm exact per-layer recovery on pretrained ImageNet-scale CNNs and ViT-B/16. The leaked spectra enable fingerprinting, lineage attribution, and improved logit-based extraction, while suppressing them destroys inference utility.
tldr: The paper breaks permutation-based model confidentiality in hybrid fully homomorphic encryption inference by showing exact recovery of linear layers from admissible queries.
motivation: Hybrid FHE inference aims to protect model confidentiality via noisy output-permuted responses and shuffle-model differential privacy, but the authors question whether this protection holds under correctness constraints.
method: They analyze the query complexity for recovering permutation-invariant layer summaries in hybrid FHE pipelines and demonstrate exact recovery of all linear layers from TFHE transcripts using a small number of queries per layer.
result: They recover ResNet-20, ImageNet-scale CNNs, and ViT-B/16 linear layers end-to-end with zero error using a bounded number of queries, and show that suppressing leaked spectra destroys inference utility.
conclusion: Permutation-based approaches are insufficient for model confidentiality in hybrid FHE inference, as input DP does not imply model confidentiality and shuffle amplification assumptions fail under correctness-bounded noise.

title: Assessment Of Non-Institutional Ai Tool Usage Among Clinicians
authors: Jarrod Mosier Sarah Pungitore
abstract: ArXiv:2609.11990v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools are increasingly accessible and have the potential to improve efficiency across clinical workflows. However, clinicians may also use non-institutional AI tools that are not provided, managed, or governed by their healthcare institutions, creating potential concerns related to privacy, security, accuracy, and clinician-AI interaction. Little is known about how clinicians currently use these tools for work-related tasks. We conducted a descriptive survey of clinicians recruited from the University of Arizona College of Medicine-Tucson and Banner University Medical Center-Tucson between May 20 and June 26, 2026. Participants reported their use of AI tool categories and the frequency with which they used AI for specific tasks across five workload categories: administrative work, clinical work, research, studying/continued education, and teaching. Forty-four respondents completed the survey. Forty-three respondents reported using AI for at least one work-related task during the preceding 6 months. Conversational AI and clinical decision support/diagnostic AI were the most used tool categories, each reported by 28 respondents. Administrative and clinical tasks demonstrated the most frequent use. AI was also used for higher-risk activities, including diagnostic assistance and clinical decision support. Non-institutional AI use was common among surveyed clinicians and extended across a broad range of work-related activities, including tasks with potential implications for clinical reasoning and patient care. Further research is needed to characterize how clinicians use these tools, how they evaluate AI-generated outputs, and how AI can be safely and effectively integrated into clinical workflows.
tldr: A descriptive survey of 44 clinicians at a US academic medical center finds that non-institutional generative AI tools are widely used across administrative, clinical, research, educational, and teaching tasks, including higher-risk diagnostic and decision-support applications.
motivation: Generative AI tools have become easily accessible to clinicians, but institutional governance, privacy, security, and accuracy safeguards may not cover tools that clinicians adopt independently, and little is known about how such non-institutional tools are actually used.
method: A descriptive survey was administered to clinicians recruited from the University of Arizona College of Medicine-Tucson and Banner University Medical Center-Tucson between May 20 and June 26, 2026, asking about AI tool categories used and frequency of use across five workload categories.
result: Forty-four clinicians completed the survey; 43 reported using AI for at least one work-related task in the prior six months, with conversational AI and clinical decision support/diagnostic AI the most common categories (28 respondents each), and administrative and clinical tasks the most frequent uses.
conclusion: Non-institutional AI use is common and spans a broad range of clinical and administrative activities, including tasks affecting clinical reasoning and patient care, motivating further work on how clinicians use and evaluate these tools and how they can be safely integrated into workflows.

title: Resonance-Enhanced Time Reflection At Photonic Temporal Interfaces
authors: Zeyuan Li, Hammam Bahurmuz, Mohamed H. Mostafa, Mohammad S. Mirmoosa, Puneet Garg, Carsten Rockstuhl, Xuchen Wang, Viktar Asadchy
abstract: ArXiv:2609.12332v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Photonic temporal interfaces enable dynamic control of light fields, yet strong time reflection at optical frequencies remains challenging because conventional approaches demand large material refractive-index changes on ultrafast timescales. Here, we introduce a resonance-assisted mechanism that harnesses both polarization energy accumulated in a dispersive medium prior to the temporal interface and strongly increased energy supplied by the modulation system. We show that, under a specific critical condition, rapidly increasing the material resonance frequency yields orders-of-magnitude stronger time-reflected power flux density than what conventional plasma-frequency modulation provides. To implement this mechanism in optical systems, we identify two routes based on dielectric and plasmonic structural resonances. For the plasmonic route, we develop an analytical effective-medium model of conducting-oxide cylinder arrays, in which localized surface-plasmon resonances transform the constituent Drude response into a geometrically tunable effective Lorentz response. Using cadmium oxide as a representative material, we predict an enhancement exceeding three orders of magnitude in the summed reflected-mode power coefficient relative to the same homogeneous material under the same modest plasma-frequency modulation, even in the presence of realistic losses. These findings establish spatial resonance engineering as an effective route to strong temporal scattering with reduced demands on intrinsic material tunability.
tldr: Introduces a resonance-assisted mechanism to enhance time reflection at photonic temporal interfaces by leveraging dispersive polarization energy and modulation energy.
motivation: Strong time reflection at optical frequencies is challenging because conventional approaches require large ultrafast refractive-index changes in materials.
method: The authors exploit a critical condition where rapidly increasing the material resonance frequency yields stronger time-reflected power, and they develop an analytical effective-medium model for conducting-oxide cylinder arrays that transform a Drude response into a geometrically tunable Lorentz response.
result: For plasmonic cadmium oxide arrays, they predict over three orders of magnitude enhancement in the summed reflected-mode power coefficient relative to homogeneous material under the same modest plasma-frequency modulation, even with realistic losses.
conclusion: Spatial resonance engineering provides an effective route to strong temporal scattering with reduced demands on intrinsic material tunability.

title: Enhanced Chiral Response Of Hybrid Photonic Structures Empowered By Mie Resonances
authors: Xingguang Liu, Wenzhe Hao, Ivan Toftul, Junqing Li, Yongkang Dong, Yuri Kivshar
abstract: ArXiv:2609.12358v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chiroptical response provides a powerful route to control light-matter interactions through light handedness, with crucial importance in polarization control, chiral sensing, and nonlinear photonics. Hybrid structures may offer a novel route to engineer such responses by coupling plasmonic field localization with dielectric Mie resonances within a single nanostructure. However, in chiral metasurfaces, hybridization has largely been treated as a means of resonance enhancement, while its role in actively reshaping and reversing intrinsic plasmonic chirality remains largely unexplored. Here, we demonstrate a hybrid metasurface in which a dielectric Mie resonance mediates enhanced chiral response of plasmonic building blocks. By coupling a Si nanocylinder to trapezoidal Au nanobars, a weak and mode-selective plasmonic chiral seed is reorganised into two opposite-handed hybrid resonances, producing near-unity circular dichroism with spectral sign flipping. Extending this mechanism to nonlinear regime, the same hybrid-mode selectivity produces strongly nonlinear chiral emission and near-unity third-harmonic generation circular dichroism of either sign. We believe these results establish plasmonic-Mie hybridization as a novel mechanism for engineering high-purity, sign-switchable linear and nonlinear chirality in compact metadevices.
tldr: A plasmonic-dielectric hybrid metasurface couples Si nanocylinders to trapezoidal Au nanobars so that dielectric Mie resonances reorganize a weak plasmonic chiral seed into two opposite-handed hybrid modes, yielding near-unity, sign-switchable circular dichroism in both linear and nonlinear regimes.
motivation: Chiroptical response enables control of light-matter interaction via light handedness, relevant for polarization control, chiral sensing and nonlinear photonics, but the role of plasmonic-dielectric hybridization in actively reshaping or reversing intrinsic plasmonic chirality remained unexplored.
method: A hybrid metasurface combining Si nanocylinders (dielectric Mie resonances) with trapezoidal Au nanobars (plasmonic building blocks) is designed and characterized, with the mechanism extended to the nonlinear regime to study chiral third-harmonic generation.
result: Mie-mediated hybridization reorganizes a weak, mode-selective plasmonic chiral seed into two opposite-handed hybrid resonances, producing near-unity circular dichroism with spectral sign flipping and strongly nonlinear chiral emission with near-unity THG circular dichroism of either sign.
conclusion: Plasmonic-Mie hybridization is established as a general mechanism for engineering high-purity, sign-switchable linear and nonlinear chirality in compact metadevices.

title: Chirality Enhances Diffusion In Disordered Environments
authors: Joshua Uhlig, Jan W\'ojcik, Ralf Metzler, Erik Kalz
abstract: ArXiv:2609.12680v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chirality, a systematic rotational bias in the motion of a particle, arises in a wide range of physical and biological systems, from charged colloids in magnetic fields to swimming bacteria near surfaces. While its effects in homogeneous environments are well understood, the interplay between chirality and structural disorder has remained largely unexplored. Here we investigate the chiral random walk on two-dimensional percolation clusters above the percolation threshold, combining numerical simulations with an analytically tractable annealed-disorder approximation. We find that the long-time diffusion coefficient depends non-monotonically on both the chirality parameter and the obstacle density: for every obstacle density above the percolation threshold, there exists an optimal chirality that enhances diffusion relative to the achiral walk. We show that the optimal chirality is set by an edge-adhering mechanism: maximum diffusion is achieved when the persistence length of the wall-adhering motion matches half the typical obstacle cluster perimeter. This yields a closed-form prediction for the optimal chirality in terms of geometric properties of the medium alone, which we verify across the full range of obstacle densities studied. The enhancement extends to first-passage statistics, where chirality shortens typical search times at strong disorder while lengthening them at weak disorder, with direct implications for biological navigation in disordered environments.
tldr: Chiral random walks on two-dimensional percolation clusters exhibit non-monotonic diffusion, with an optimal chirality that enhances diffusion by matching the persistence length to obstacle cluster perimeter.
motivation: Chirality is common in physical and biological systems, but its interplay with structural disorder in diffusive transport has remained largely unexplored.
method: The authors combine numerical simulations with an analytically tractable annealed-disorder approximation to study chiral random walks on percolation clusters above the percolation threshold.
result: The long-time diffusion coefficient depends non-monotonically on chirality and obstacle density; for every density above threshold, an optimal chirality enhances diffusion, and this optimum is set by an edge-adhering mechanism yielding a closed-form geometric prediction.
conclusion: Chirality can enhance diffusion and shorten first-passage times at strong disorder while lengthening them at weak disorder, with implications for biological navigation in disordered environments.

title: Admm And Linearized Admm For Weakly Convex Minimization
authors: Shenghan Mei, Chengyu Ke, Yifei Lou, Miju Ahn
abstract: ArXiv:2609.12167v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a class of weakly convex optimization problems in which the objective is the sum of a smooth convex term and a weakly convex term that may be nonsmooth. To exploit this structure, we develop a splitting technique based on the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM), which decouples the minimization of the two components into tractable subproblems. Because the update associated with the smooth term may require an inner iterative solver, we further linearize this term, yielding a linearized ADMM (LADMM) scheme with an inexpensive one-step update. Under mild conditions, we establish the subsequence convergence of both ADMM and LADMM methods to directional stationary solutions, which are equivalent to critical points and Clarke stationary solutions for our weakly convex problem. Numerical experiments on two low-dimensional test functions and a high-dimensional logarithmic regularized logistic regression model demonstrate that the proposed approaches are computationally efficient and produce solutions of comparable quality to baseline methods.
tldr: The paper develops ADMM and linearized ADMM splitting schemes for weakly convex optimization problems that decompose into a smooth convex term plus a nonsmooth weakly convex term.
motivation: Many modern optimization problems involve nonsmooth weakly convex objectives for which standard convex splitting methods do not directly apply, motivating convergent algorithms that remain computationally cheap per iteration.
method: The authors apply an ADMM splitting that decouples the two objective components, then linearize the smooth term to obtain an LADMM variant with a single-step inner update; convergence is analyzed via directional stationarity.
result: Both ADMM and LADMM are shown to converge (subsequence convergence) to directional stationary points, which coincide with critical and Clarke stationary solutions for the weakly convex setting; experiments on low-dimensional tests and high-dimensional log-regularized logistic regression show efficiency competitive with baselines.
conclusion: The proposed schemes provide efficient, provably convergent tools for weakly convex minimization, though the work is purely in classical continuous optimization and has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: A Localization Framework For $\mathbb{T}^m$-Invariant Toeplitz Algebras: Applications To Gelfand Theory
authors: Miguel Angel Rodriguez Rodriguez
abstract: ArXiv:2609.12368v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study [MATH]-invariant Toeplitz operators on weighted Bergman spaces over the unit ball. A natural unitary transformation represents each such operator as a direct sum of restrictions of Toeplitz operators acting on a polyball. Under an [MATH]-valued angular continuity assumption, the corresponding symbols extend from [MATH] to a norm-continuous family indexed by the maximal ideal space of the [MATH]-algebra generated by [MATH]-quasi-radial Toeplitz operators. This extension yields a localization framework for Toeplitz operator algebras. As an application, we consider commutative Banach algebras obtained by adjoining Toeplitz operators whose symbols are invariant under mixed unitary and circle actions. We identify their local quotient algebras on finite-coordinate strata and at infinity and use these identifications to describe their maximal ideal spaces and Gelfand transforms explicitly.
tldr: This paper develops a localization framework for T^m-invariant Toeplitz operator algebras on weighted Bergman spaces and applies it to describe their maximal ideal spaces and Gelfand transforms.
motivation: The study aims to understand the structure of Toeplitz operator algebras invariant under torus actions, extending classical Gelfand theory to these noncommutative settings.
method: The authors use a unitary transformation to represent T^m-invariant Toeplitz operators as direct sums of restricted Toeplitz operators on a polyball, and then impose an angular continuity condition to extend symbols to the maximal ideal space.
result: They obtain a localization framework that identifies local quotient algebras on finite-coordinate strata and at infinity, yielding explicit descriptions of maximal ideal spaces and Gelfand transforms for certain commutative Banach algebras.
conclusion: The framework provides a systematic way to analyze T^m-invariant Toeplitz algebras, with potential applications in operator theory and harmonic analysis, but it is not directly connected to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Polynomial Growth Of Bohnenblust--Hille Constants On The Hamming Cube
authors: Paata Ivanisvili
abstract: ArXiv:2609.12427v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the Bohnenblust--Hille constants for Walsh polynomials on the Hamming cube grow at most polynomially in the degree. More precisely, there is an absolute constant [MATH] such that every [MATH] of degree at most [MATH] satisfies $[MATH][MATH]27$ is not optimized.
tldr: The paper proves that Bohnenblust--Hille constants for Walsh polynomials on the Hamming cube grow at most polynomially in the degree.
motivation: Understanding the growth of Bohnenblust--Hille constants is important in harmonic analysis and the theory of Boolean functions, with connections to inequalities on the Hamming cube.
method: The author uses analytic and combinatorial techniques to bound the Bohnenblust--Hille constants for Walsh polynomials of degree at most n.
result: An absolute constant exists such that the Bohnenblust--Hille constant for degree-n Walsh polynomials is bounded polynomially in n.
conclusion: This establishes polynomial growth of the constants, improving upon previous bounds and contributing to the analysis of inequalities on the Hamming cube.

title: Sharp Error Estimates For A Fully Discrete Finite Element Method For Semilinear SPDEs With Multiplicative Noise And Nonsmooth Initial Data
authors: Lok Pati Tripathi Jitendra Nath Naik
abstract: ArXiv:2609.12485v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This article establishes sharp strong error estimates for the fully discrete approximation of semilinear parabolic stochastic partial differential equations (SPDEs) driven by multiplicative noise and subject to nonsmooth initial data. The spatial discretization is based on a standard finite element method, coupled with the linearly implicit Euler scheme in time. By mapping the diffusion operator into negative fractional spaces, our framework accommodates both trace-class and space-time white noise. For nonsmooth initial data, by decoupling the noise regularity parameter [MATH] from the initial data regularity parameter [MATH], we derive sharp regularity estimates that isolate the exact loss of initial regularity into an integrable temporal singularity. Furthermore, we establish sharp strong convergence rates of [MATH] for [MATH] away from [MATH]. Finally, we consider physically relevant stochastic models, such as the modified Langmuir fractional surface coverage model and the parabolic Anderson model, in our numerical experiments to confirm the theoretical convergence rates.
tldr: The paper derives sharp strong error estimates for a fully discrete finite element method applied to semilinear parabolic SPDEs with multiplicative noise and nonsmooth initial data.
motivation: Numerical schemes for semilinear SPDEs with nonsmooth initial data and multiplicative noise lack sharp error bounds that correctly decouple noise regularity from initial-data regularity.
method: A standard finite element spatial discretization combined with a linearly implicit Euler time-stepping scheme, analyzed via mapping the diffusion operator into negative fractional Sobolev spaces to handle trace-class and space-time white noise.
result: Sharp regularity estimates isolating the loss of initial regularity into an integrable temporal singularity, plus sharp strong convergence rates for the scheme away from singular limits.
conclusion: Numerical experiments on the modified Langmuir fractional surface coverage model and the parabolic Anderson model confirm the theoretical convergence rates.

title: Quaternion Quadratic Phase Dunkl Transform: Its Properties And Uncertainty Principle
authors: Akhilesh Prasad, Debabrata Biswal, Manab Kundu
abstract: ArXiv:2609.12516v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by the wide applications of the quadratic phase integral transform in signal processing, optics, and time frequency analysis, in this paper we develop a new integral transform called the quaternion quadratic phase Dunkl transform (QQPDT). We present a detailed study of its fundamental properties. In particular, we establish continuity, linearity, scaling, modulation, Riemann Lebesgue result, inversion formula, and Parsevals identity. In addition, we estab lish Heisenberg and Donoho-Stark-type uncertainty principles for the QQPDT. Finally, we develop a signal recovery algorithm in the QQPDT domain. The proposed method enables the reconstruction of missing signal information from partial observations under suitable localization conditions.
tldr: The paper introduces and studies a quaternion quadratic phase Dunkl transform, proving basic properties and uncertainty principles and applying it to signal recovery.
motivation: The quadratic phase integral transform has applications in signal processing, optics, and time-frequency analysis, motivating an extension to a quaternionic Dunkl setting.
method: The authors define the quaternion quadratic phase Dunkl transform and derive fundamental properties such as continuity, linearity, scaling, modulation, Riemann-Lebesgue lemma, inversion, and Parseval identity, along with Heisenberg and Donoho-Stark uncertainty principles.
result: They establish the theoretical properties and uncertainty principles of the transform and develop a signal recovery algorithm for reconstructing missing information from partial observations under localization conditions.
conclusion: The proposed QQPDT provides a new mathematical tool for signal analysis, but its focus is classical integral-transform theory rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Opening The Strategic Pandora Box: Conditional Transaction Mechanisms
authors: Yonatan Sompolinsky, Ori Newman, Xintong Wang, David Parkes
abstract: ArXiv:2609.12197v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conditional transaction engines (CTEs) execute conditional instructions for offline users. This paper formalizes the mechanism-design problem within each engine invocation. A conditional transaction mechanism (CTM) decides which pending conditions to evaluate first because each evaluation delays the eventual write. We model this problem as Strategic Pandora, a discounted variant of the Pandora's box model with independent Bernoulli boxes. Agents report privately assessed success probabilities and, in the full model, values for the write action. We propose the reported-Weitzman mechanism (RW) and the reported-values second-price mechanism (RWSP). To compare revenue without a common prior, we introduce dynamic No-Betting Revenue. Under the stated competition and equilibrium conditions, every qualifying pure equilibrium of RW or RWSP earns a constant fraction of its corresponding dynamic NBR benchmark.
tldr: The paper formalizes conditional transaction mechanisms as a strategic variant of Pandora's box and proposes mechanisms that achieve a constant fraction of a dynamic no-betting revenue benchmark.
motivation: Conditional transaction engines execute conditional instructions for offline users, and deciding which pending conditions to evaluate first affects write delays and revenue.
method: The authors model the problem as Strategic Pandora with independent Bernoulli boxes, where agents privately report success probabilities and values, and analyze the reported-Weitzman mechanism and a reported-values second-price mechanism.
result: They introduce dynamic No-Betting Revenue to compare revenue without a common prior and show that every qualifying pure equilibrium of the proposed mechanisms earns a constant fraction of its corresponding benchmark.
conclusion: The work provides a mechanism-design framework for conditional transaction systems, with revenue guarantees under specified competition and equilibrium conditions.

title: Evaluating Practical Enumeration And Blocking Attacks On The Snowflake Circumvention System
authors: Linden Chen, Ryan Sangha, Cecylia Bocovich, Ram Sundara Raman
abstract: ArXiv:2609.12242v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Proxy-based Internet censorship circumvention tools like Snowflake rely on large, dynamic pools of third-party proxies to resist IP-based blocking. We focus on two assumptions underpinning the security of Snowflake: that adversaries cannot easily enumerate proxy IPs, and that blocking those proxies would incur unacceptable collateral damage. In this paper, we test these assumptions by studying practical enumeration and blocking attacks against Snowflake conducted by malicious clients. We combine bounded, ethical real-world measurements with large-scale simulation to evaluate both present-day enumeration and blocking risk and broader attacker capabilities. Over 48 days of real-world measurements from May--June 2025, our attack enumerated over 21,000 unique proxy IP addresses belonging to almost 1,000 autonomous systems. Despite this high number, we find that proxy churn limits the overall effectiveness of enumeration over time, and reduces the impact on clients of individual proxy addresses being blocked. However, at the network level, blocking the top 1% of observed autonomous systems blocks more than 30% of observed Snowflakes while affecting 0% of Tranco Top 100 domains and ~2.5% of Top 1M domains. We discover that the broker's load-aware matching reveals stable, high-capacity proxies to attackers early, especially during periods of elevated demand such as the censorship even in Iran of June 2025, subsequently exposing the networks that contribute disproportionately to system connectivity. In simulation, increasing attacker scale sharply improves both enumeration and blocking success, while higher proxy churn significantly reduces blocking effectiveness. We conclude by discussing and evaluating practical mitigations, some of which have been integrated into Snowflake.
tldr: The paper empirically evaluates enumeration and IP-blocking attacks against the Snowflake censorship circumvention system, finding that broker load-aware matching exposes stable high-capacity proxies while churn mitigates long-term blocking effectiveness.
motivation: Snowflake's security rests on two assumptions: that adversaries cannot easily enumerate proxy IPs and that blocking them would cause unacceptable collateral damage. The authors test whether these assumptions hold in practice.
method: The authors combine 48 days of bounded, ethical real-world measurements (May–June 2025) from malicious-client vantage points with large-scale simulation to assess present-day and future attacker enumeration and blocking capabilities.
result: They enumerated over 21,000 unique proxy IPs across nearly 1,000 autonomous systems; blocking the top 1% of ASes would block over 30% of observed Snowflakes while affecting 0% of Tranco Top 100 and ~2.5% of Top 1M domains, and broker load-aware matching leaks stable high-capacity proxies during demand spikes such as Iran's June 2025 censorship event.
conclusion: Enumeration and blocking risks are real but partly offset by proxy churn; the authors propose and evaluate practical mitigations, some of which have already been integrated into Snowflake.

title: Breakdown Of Multipole Expansion In Emergent Electromagnetism
authors: Tom Ben-Ami, Markus Heyl, Roderich Moessner
abstract: ArXiv:2609.12063v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We find a striking departure from simple electrostatics in a family of two-dimensional lattice models whose effective description takes the form of an emergent electromagnetism: a high-order multipolar charge configuration can induce an electric field characteristic of a order multipole. Studying the archetypical hardcore dimer and U(1) spin-1/2 link models, we trace this to a breakdown of the superposition principle: for dense charge configurations, there can be a nonlinear suppression, or even enhancement, of the far field compared to the linear expectation. Our work establishes that microscopic lattice-scale constraints in models for emergent electromagnetism can change the far-field behaviour to differ from often utilized long-wavelength descriptions in standard effective continuum models.
tldr: Microscopic lattice constraints in emergent electromagnetism can break the superposition principle, causing far fields to deviate from standard multipole expansion predictions.
motivation: Standard effective continuum descriptions often assume linear electrostatics, but it is unclear whether lattice-scale constraints in emergent gauge theories preserve this long-wavelength behavior.
method: The authors study hardcore dimer and U(1) spin-1/2 link models on two-dimensional lattices, analyzing how dense charge configurations induce far electric fields compared to linear multipole expectations.
result: They find a breakdown of the superposition principle: high-order multipolar configurations can produce fields characteristic of lower-order multipoles, with nonlinear suppression or enhancement of the far field.
conclusion: Microscopic lattice constraints can qualitatively alter far-field behavior in emergent electromagnetism, invalidating simple continuum multipole expansions for dense charge configurations.

title: Disordered Hyperuniform Modulated Phases And The Cosmic Web From One Free Energy
authors: Fausto Martelli
abstract: ArXiv:2609.11988v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Disordered hyperuniformity spans twenty-five orders of magnitude, from the microscopic world of soft and condensed matter to the distribution of matter in the universe. We introduce a free-energy functional with no adjustable coupling, a phase-field-crystal ordering term and a Newtonian tail, and show that its two kinetic limits generate two of these structures. Under conserved overdamped dynamics it arrests in a bicontinuous labyrinth of the kind found in confined fluids, block copolymers, active matter and vegetation patterns, which is a class III disordered hyperuniform state; under inertial dynamics in an expanding background it generates a cosmic web whose tidal skeleton matches that of gravity alone to within [MATH] in every morphological class. In both limits the suppressed long-wavelength fluctuations are inherited from the initial condition rather than made by the dynamics: the large-scale exponent of the arrested state equals the primordial one, and gravity rescales the infrared spectrum by the linear growth factor to better than one per cent over a factor [MATH] of growth. The two sectors are continuously connected, and their distance is measurable: once the ordering modulation saturates, its mean-field back-reaction leaves the medium with a residual pressure proportional to [MATH] that suppresses the growth of the largest scales by a smooth factor and vanishes in the cold-matter limit [MATH].
tldr: A single free-energy functional is shown to produce both a class III disordered hyperuniform labyrinth phase under conserved overdamped dynamics and a cosmic web under inertial dynamics in an expanding background.
motivation: Disordered hyperuniformity appears across 25 orders of magnitude, from soft condensed matter to the large-scale structure of the universe, motivating a unified description linking these seemingly disparate structures.
method: A free-energy functional with no adjustable coupling, combining a phase-field-crystal ordering term and a Newtonian tail, is evolved under two kinetic limits: conserved overdamped dynamics and inertial dynamics in an expanding background.
result: The conserved limit arrests in a bicontinuous labyrinth identified as a class III disordered hyperuniform state, while the inertial limit reproduces a cosmic web whose tidal skeleton matches gravity-only simulations to within a small deviation; long-wavelength suppression is inherited from initial conditions.
conclusion: The two sectors are continuously connected by a measurable distance, with a residual pressure from mean-field back-reaction suppressing the growth of the largest scales and vanishing in the cold-matter limit.

title: Models And Measures Of Statistical Physics And Sociophysics For Fracture Mechanics And Earthquake Dynamics: An Introduction
authors: Sudip Sarkar, Soumyajyoti Biswas, Bikas K. Chakrabarti
abstract: ArXiv:2609.12109v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The breaking or fracture of materials and damages or devastations due to earthquakes have caught our attention since the earliest stage of human civilization. In fact, at around 1500, Leonardo Da Vinci made the pioneering observation that, unlike elastic constants (formalized later by Hooke in 1678) of the materials, the tensile (breaking) strengths of nominally identical iron wires decrease drastically with their length, indicating the vanishing breaking strength of materials in the large size limit, suggesting the impossibility of constructing arbitrarily large structures. This was the first observation that unlike the elasticity of disordered materials, which remains defined in the thermodynamic limit (self averaging statistics), the breaking properties of the disordered materials have extreme (non self averaging) statistics.
